approach: Root cause: the planner brief tells the planner in prose to list every caller and mode of what it changes (`OPEN_QUESTION_RULE`, `crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs:66-68`) but never shows it the callers of the functions in the deliverable files. The brief's deliverable facts are only path, exists and bytes (`DeliverableFact`, planner.rs:16-21; built at `crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs:121-129`). The planner has Read, Grep and Glob only (`planning_grant`, planning.rs:701-708), so it finds callers by search and stops at the first paths it meets, for example missing the `[parallel] max_concurrency` path into landing. No rule asks it to tabulate each exit of a changed stage. Fix at the input, not as a refusal: (1) in athena-core, a new `pub(super) fn deliverable_facts` on `Athena` replaces the inline loop at planning.rs:121-129. For each existing `.rs` deliverable it lists the non-test `fn` names, reads every `.rs` blob of the base commit through `self.git.ls_tree` and `cat_blob`, builds one index of call-like tokens (identifier directly followed by `(`, not preceded by `fn`, comment lines skipped), and returns per function the call sites in other files (`path:line`, non-test paths first, capped at 4) plus counts of other-file and same-file sites. A non-Rust or missing deliverable gets `callers: None`. (2) In athena-context, `DeliverableFact` gains `callers: Option<Vec<FunctionCallers>>`, and `planner_brief` renders under each Rust deliverable a labelled, approximate list: functions with callers elsewhere (file:line), functions called only in their own file, and functions with no callers found, so a deliverable with none shows 'no callers found'. (3) A new `EXITS_RULE` const is added to the Report after `CODE_CLAIMS_RULE`, for both the first-round and the revision brief, and says a plan that changes a stage or core flow must tabulate every exit (success, fail, error, hold, interrupt) with the file:line that handles it, the state it leaves and the code that reads that state. (4) CHANGELOG.md names the root cause. `admission.rs` and the reading checks are untouched, so the share of past accepted readings newly refused is 0%.

decisions.choice: Compute the caller list in Athena from the base commit and put it in the brief as data, labelled approximate and a starting list the planner must extend.
decisions.reason: The failure class is missing information, not missing rules: the prose rule exists (planner.rs:66-68, :91-92) and the planner has no git or shell (planning.rs:701-708). A computed list puts the adjacent callers in front of it before round 1. The label keeps it from treating a textual search as complete.

rejected.option: Refuse a plan whose dependents omit a caller found by Athena's search
rejected.why: The brief says a refusal rule is allowed only when the information cannot prevent the failure. A textual search has false positives (same method name on another type), so a refusal would block valid plans. The reading checks and admission.rs are out of scope.

rejected.option: Tell the planner to Grep for callers more thoroughly (prose only)
rejected.why: That is the existing rule, and nine jobs show it is not enough.

decisions.choice: Match call-like tokens (`name(` not preceded by `fn`) in one pass over all `.rs` blobs, building a name-to-sites index.
decisions.reason: It needs no parser, runs in time linear in the source, and works on a fixture of a few files. The tests.rs deliverable is about 500 KB with hundreds of functions, so a per-function scan of every line would be too slow. Using the same index for all functions keeps cost at one read of the tree per round.

rejected.option: Parse Rust with syn or a call graph
rejected.why: athena-core has no syn dependency (only the crates in the system facts' Cargo reach list); a new dependency is more than the smallest design needs and would still not resolve trait calls.

rejected.option: Run `git grep` per function through Git
rejected.why: `Git` exposes no grep (only ls_tree, show_file, cat_blob; crates/athena-git/src/lib.rs:516-549), and one spawn per function is slow for large deliverables.

decisions.choice: Add a new field `callers` to `DeliverableFact` rather than reuse `bytes` or `exists`.
decisions.reason: `DeliverableFact` (planner.rs:14-21) documents only path, existence and size; none of them means callers. `Option` distinguishes 'not computed' (non-Rust or missing file) from 'computed, none found'.

rejected.option: Put the callers into the existing `path` string or a separate parameter of `PlannerInputs`
rejected.why: It would split one deliverable's facts across two inputs and break the one-line-per-deliverable rendering that briefs.rs:2812 pins.

decisions.choice: Show callers in other files first and only count same-file call sites; skip `#[test]` functions and stop at a column-0 `#[cfg(test)]`; list at most 30 functions with callers elsewhere per deliverable and say how many more.
decisions.reason: The failure was missing adjacent paths in other files. Test helpers and same-file calls would swamp a 500 KB tests.rs deliverable. Caps keep the brief small (worst case about 6 KB per Rust deliverable, an estimate, not measured).

rejected.why: Common names such as `new` have thousands of sites and would bury the useful ones.

decisions.choice: Add `EXITS_RULE` as its own const after `CODE_CLAIMS_RULE` in the Report, one line without newlines, pinned by a test like the other rules.
decisions.reason: The latest introspection (job 20261115-202532-6mng) names an exit table for a changed stage as the missing piece. The rule sits where the other planner rules are, so it appears exactly once in both the first-round and revision brief (planner.rs:168-171 is shared by both).

rejected.option: Put the exit table wording in prompts/planner.md
rejected.why: Out of scope: the prompt files have almost no token headroom (planner 1188 of 1200 in docs/system-facts.md).

rejected.option: Have admission.rs check the plan for an exits table
rejected.why: Out of scope and a refusal rule. Whether a table is complete cannot be judged by code, so the critic reads it.

files.purpose: Add `FunctionCallers` and the `callers: Option<Vec<FunctionCallers>>` field to `DeliverableFact`, with a doc comment naming the root cause. Render the callers under each Rust deliverable in `planner_brief`. Add `EXITS_RULE` and append it to the Report.
Export `FunctionCallers`; add `callers: None` to the two `DeliverableFact` literals; add the callers rendering test and the exits-rule test; update the Report size bound test.
Add `Athena::deliverable_facts` and the pure helpers (`function_names`, `call_index`, caller selection) with unit tests; replace the inline loop in `planning_round` with it.
Add the git-fixture tests for `deliverable_facts` and for the planner prompt carrying the callers (names beginning `deliverable_callers`).
One entry under [Unreleased] / Changed naming the root cause, the change, its limits and the tests.

steps: In crates/athena-context/src/briefs/planner.rs add `pub struct FunctionCallers { pub function: String, pub elsewhere: usize, pub same_file: usize, pub sites: Vec<String> }` (sites are `path:line`) and `pub callers: Option<Vec<FunctionCallers>>` on `DeliverableFact`, both with doc comments that state the root cause (the brief gave no computed callers or exits, only prose), that None means not computed (not a Rust file or missing) and that the list is approximate. Export `FunctionCallers` next to `DeliverableFact` in briefs.rs:26.

In planner.rs render the callers inside the Deliverables loop of `planner_brief` (lines 132-144): after the `exists` line, for `Some(list)` write an indented intro line saying it is a textual search of the base snapshot's Rust files for `name(`, approximate and not complete, to be extended with Grep; then one line per function with callers elsewhere (`- \`f\`: a.rs:10, b.rs:20 (+3 more)`, at most 30, then '+N more functions with callers elsewhere'), one line `called only inside this file: \`g\` (2 sites), ...`, and one line `no callers found: \`h\`, ...`; an empty list says the file declares no functions. Keep the text free of `## Report`. Add `pub(super) const EXITS_RULE: &str` (one line, no newline, with a doc comment that names the root cause and says it is information, not a refusal) requiring a plan that adds or changes a stage or core flow to tabulate every exit (success, fail, error, hold, interrupt) of each new or changed stage with the file:line that handles it, the state or record it leaves and the code that reads that state. Append `\n\n{EXITS_RULE}` after `{CODE_CLAIMS_RULE}` in the Report format string (planner.rs:170).

In crates/athena-core/src/run/planning.rs add private pure helpers: `function_names(source) -> Vec<String>` (a `fn name` token not inside a line comment; skip a function whose previous non-blank line is `#[test]`; stop at a line equal to `#[cfg(test)]`), and `call_index(files: &[(String, String)]) -> BTreeMap<String, Vec<(usize, usize)>>` (identifier directly followed by `(`, not preceded by the token `fn`, comment lines skipped, line numbers from 1). Then `pub(super) fn deliverable_facts(&self, treeish: &str, paths: &[String]) -> Result<Vec<DeliverableFact>>`: for each path call `self.git.show_file`; for an existing `.rs` file compute `callers` from the index built once per call (lazily, from `self.git.ls_tree(treeish)` blob entries ending `.rs`, bytes through `self.git.cat_blob(oid)`, lossy UTF-8); other paths get `callers: None`. Order sites non-test paths first (a path with `tests` as a component or file stem is a test path), then path and line, capped at 4. Use it in `planning_round` in place of lines 121-129 with `accepted.deliverables.iter().map(|d| d.0.clone())`.

Add tests in planning.rs's test module for the pure helpers (a `#[test]` fn and a `fn` in a comment are skipped; a `fn name(` declaration is not a call; `x.name(` and `Foo::name(` are calls; text after `#[cfg(test)]` is ignored). In crates/athena-core/src/run/tests.rs add `deliverable_callers_lists_both_callers_and_shows_a_deliverable_with_none` (real git repo, direct call to `deliverable_facts("HEAD", ...)`) and `deliverable_callers_reach_the_planner_prompt` (reader deliverables replaced as in `run_planned_behavior`, the first planner prompt in `calls` carries both caller lines).

In crates/athena-context/src/briefs.rs add `callers: None` to the two literals at lines 2780-2790; add `a_planner_brief_lists_the_callers_of_each_deliverable` and `the_planner_brief_requires_an_exit_table_once_in_both_rounds` (first-round and revision brief, count 1, wording needles); update the Report size bound at lines 4164-4179 to add `EXITS_RULE.len() + 2` and the matching message.

Add the CHANGELOG.md bullet at the head of `### Changed` under `## [Unreleased]` (CHANGELOG.md:10-12): root cause, the three changes, limits (approximate textual search, caps, the planner may ignore the table, the saving in round-cap stops is not measured), no refusal rule (0% newly refused) and the test filters. Do not touch docs/system-facts.md (briefs sit outside the budgets), admission.rs, any prompt .md file, athena.toml or records/.

Run `cargo fmt --all`, then `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings`, `cargo test -p athena-context` and `cargo test -p athena-core` and fix findings (the checks are fmt, clippy and `cargo test --locked`).

risks.risk: The textual search finds false callers (a method with the same name on another type) or misses callers through macros, trait objects or paths split across lines, so the planner may trust the list too much.
risks.mitigation: The brief labels the list as approximate and a starting list to extend with Grep, and the existing `OPEN_QUESTION_RULE` and `CODE_CLAIMS_RULE` still require the planner to cite what it read. Tests pin the label wording.

risks.risk: Brief size or time grows: one `cat-file` per `.rs` blob per planner call (about a few hundred spawns) and up to about 6 KB of text per Rust deliverable (estimate, not measured).
risks.mitigation: One read of the tree per call; functions shown are capped at 30 with a 'more' count and sites at 4; test functions and same-file sites are only counted. Planner calls take minutes, so a read of the tree is small by comparison. A git error still ends the call exactly as the old `show_file` call did.

risks.risk: Common function names (`new`, `run`) make the list noisy for a deliverable such as a large tests.rs.
risks.mitigation: Test functions are skipped, other-file sites come first with non-test paths ahead of test paths, and a function with only same-file calls is folded into one line.

risks.risk: A model planner may still ignore the exit table; only the critic reads it.
risks.mitigation: This is information, not a refusal; the rule says what to tabulate and where to cite. Whether it reduces round-cap stops is not measured here and the changelog says so.

risks.risk: Adding the rule makes the Report size bound test (briefs.rs:4164) fail until it is updated.
risks.mitigation: Step 5 updates the bound to count `EXITS_RULE`; the test run in the demonstrations catches a miss.

The CHANGELOG entry under Unreleased/Changed and the doc comment on `FunctionCallers`/`DeliverableFact` and `EXITS_RULE` each state the cause: the brief gave no computed callers or exits for the functions in the deliverable files, only prose, so plans skipped adjacent paths such as `[parallel] max_concurrency` into landing. demonstrations.method: New test in briefs.rs next to `planner_briefs_number_criteria_flag_governance_and_list_the_verifiers_commands`. It builds `planner_inputs(None)` and replaces `deliverable_facts` with a Rust deliverable whose `callers` hold three functions: one with two other-file sites, one called only in its own file and one with none. It calls `planner_brief` and takes the text between the Deliverables heading and the next `## `. It asserts each `path:line` is there, the '+N more' count, the only-in-this-file line and the 'no callers found' line. It also asserts a deliverable with `callers: None` (CHANGELOG.md) has no callers line and that the existing `- athena.toml: exists, 1234 bytes` line still holds.

demonstrations.method: Two tests. (a) A unit test in planning.rs's test module for the pure helpers (`function_names`, `call_index`) on in-memory strings. (b) In run/tests.rs, build a real git repo with `repo_with_config` and `commit_file`: `crates/x/src/core.rs` declares `fn land_job()` and `fn unused_helper()`; `crates/x/src/a.rs` and `crates/x/src/b.rs` each call `land_job(`; `crates/x/src/other.rs` is a second deliverable with no callers; README.md is a non-Rust deliverable. It builds `athena_with(...)` and calls `athena.deliverable_facts("HEAD", &paths)`. Asserts that `land_job` lists `crates/x/src/a.rs:N` and `crates/x/src/b.rs:M` with the right line numbers, that `unused_helper` and the `other.rs` functions are present with zero sites (not omitted) and that README.md has `callers: None`. A second test uses the fake driver path of `run_planned` with the reader's deliverables replaced (as `run_planned_behavior` does at run/tests.rs:1379-1386) to point at `crates/x/src/core.rs`, and asserts the first planner prompt in `calls` contains both `a.rs:` and `b.rs:` lines, which shows `planning_round` is wired.
demonstrations.observes: Both caller files are listed by file:line; a deliverable with no callers reads 'no callers found'; the planner's real prompt carries them.
